NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

NOV 1 O 1938

Seaforths, Marines
Injured Improving

The condition of the six members
of the British Forces detained in
hospital as a result of the recent
bombing of Ma Jackson's tavern on
Bubbling Well Road, was reported to
be very satisfactory yesterday. The
men: Ptes. Sutherland, Duffy, Ritchie,
of the Seaforths, Pte. Newman of the
Royal Marines, who are being treated
at the British Military Hospital, and
Ptes. Pitt and Ray of the Royal
Marines, who are still at the
General Hospital, are expected to
be returned to their units shortly.
Meanwhile police investigations
still continue into the bombing of
the bar and the report that a for-
eigner threw the glass bomb into the
establishment is being followed up.
Statements taken at the time of the
bombing were varied owing to the
confusion which reigned. Most of
the men in the bar at the time,
however, stated that the missile
was thrown by a Chinese who
opened the door and hurled the
object inside.

苏格兰海福尔团士兵、皇家海军陆战队员
伤情好转

据报道，昨日因近期静安寺路杰克逊夫人酒馆遭炸弹袭击而住院的六名英军人员状况非常良好。这些人包括：在英军医院接受治疗的苏格兰海福尔团士兵 Sutherland、Duffy、Ritchie 三等兵，皇家海军陆战队 Newman 二等兵，以及仍在广慈医院（General Hospital）的皇家海军陆战队 Pitt 和 Ray 二等兵，预计不久后将返回各自部队。与此同时，警方对该酒吧爆炸案的调查仍在继续，有关一名外国人向店内投掷玻璃炸弹的报告正在跟进中。由于当时现场一片混乱，所取得的供词各不相同。然而，当时在酒吧内的大多数人表示，投掷物是由一名打开门并将物体扔进屋内的中国人所为。

3.

静安寺路292号被投掷炸弹案。

自就本案提交第2号日志以来，负责调查的侦探未获得任何有用信息。经查实，提篮桥路助理副警察局长（D.A.P.M.）Cole 上尉从其管辖下的宪兵处未获得任何有用信息，这些宪兵每日与当地酒吧等地的海陆军士兵接触。（见附呈报告）。

中国报贩 Wong Kei Sung 每日在静安寺路292号酒吧外卖报，刑事侦缉股警员345号已与其接触，但他并未见到他声称投掷炸弹的人。

静安寺路294号的 D.R. Weerappuli 未见到他指控投掷炸弹的那名中国人。D.S.I. Macahy 及其职员在麦格理戈路车站寻找 Max Herman Schlinder 的努力失败，杰克逊夫人的儿子 Bobby Jackson 能认出此人，但也未能找到他。一旦找到他，将就此事对其进行讯问。

具名者每日与杰克逊夫人联系，但未了解到对侦探有太大帮助的情况。

她表示，在投掷炸弹之前，一名叫 J. Morgan 的人曾提出收购她的生意，霞飞路上海酒吧（Pops place）的老板也曾提出同样要求。她拒绝了出售生意的提议，正如

of the Neptune Tavern, M Gaby, 72 Bubbling Well Road
who was also offered a price for his business by a
person representing a Russian recently arrived from
Tientsin.

Since the throwing of the bomb at 292 Bubbling Well
J. Morgan has frequented the place daily and has settled
an account outstanding since March 1938. He appears
in funds but prior to the throwing of the bomb failed
to visit the bar.

Mrs. Jackson has no connection with "New Deal Bar",
26/8 Rue de Consulat or the "Frisco Cafe", 33 Avenue
Edward VII and her employees have not worked at either
of these places.

Although not treated well by her husband whom she
divorced a considerable time ago, Mrs. Jackson does not
think he or "Max Schlinder would try to ruin her business
by having the bomb thrown at her address.

Had this bomb throwing been an attempt to injure
British Forces a hand grenade or "stick" bomb would have
been used, the intent being to kill and bombs would not
have been thrown into New Deal Bar and Frisco Cafe when
no British Forces were present.

If bomb was thrown by parties interested in purchasing
Mrs. Jackson's business would the New Deal and Frisco
Cafe have been victimised? It is doubtful and motive for
the throwing of the bomb is yet unknown.

静安寺路72号 Neptune Tavern 的老板 M Gaby 所做的那样，后者也被一名代表最近从天津抵达的俄国人的买家出价收购其生意。

自静安寺路292号发生投掷炸弹事件以来，J. Morgan 每日光顾该地，并结清了自1938年3月以来拖欠的账目。他似乎资金充裕，但在投掷炸弹事件发生前却未曾光顾该酒吧。

杰克逊夫人与领事馆路26/8号的“New Deal Bar”或爱多亚路33号的“Frisco Cafe”没有任何关联，她的雇员也未在这两处地方工作过。

尽管她很久以前离婚的丈夫待她不好，但杰克逊夫人认为他或“Max Schlinder”不会试图通过在她的地址投掷炸弹来毁掉她的生意。

如果这次投掷炸弹是企图伤害英军，就会使用手榴弹或“柄式”炸弹，其意图是杀人；而且当没有英军在场时，炸弹也不会被投掷到 New Deal Bar 和 Frisco Cafe。

如果炸弹是由有意购买杰克逊夫人生意的一方投掷的，那么 New Deal 和 Frisco Cafe 会成为受害者吗？这值得怀疑，投掷炸弹的动机尚不清楚。

On 9-11-38 the undersigned received from Louza
Station an anonymous letter that had been addressed to
"The Inspector Louza Police Station Local. The address
was typewritten on a buff coloured envelope 7" by 4½"
and same bore post office markings proving it had been
posted at Nanking Road Post Office 7-11-38, marked
delivered 8-11-38. The contents of the letter were as
follows:-

Shanghai, 7th November, 1938.
The Inspector,
You will find out the key about
the matter of last night Bubbling Well Road's
Bomb. Hurry to the follows:-
Sun Tson Lian, (Chinese)
Cathay (Kou Tai) Trading Co.
New China State Bank Bldg.,
356, Peking Road
Excuse me for deleting my name and
resident.
Yours Truly,
XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

same being typed on an oblong piece of paper 5½" by 3½"
bearing water marks "Nepal made in" (here paper is cut
off).

C.D.S. 19 was instructed to make discreet enquiries
re Sun Tson Lian at 356 Peking Road but after attending
the offices of the Cathay Trading Co. at that address
several times was unsuccessful in obtaining information,
but from the landlord of 356 Peking Road it was learned
that the Cathay Trading Coy. had terminated business.
It was ascertained that the guarantor of Cathay Trading
Company was Tsang Ts Ju (張世), 54/136 Amoy Road.

经走访，他表示 Cathay Trading Company 由三名年轻中国男子组成，分别是 Tsang Ts Joong (張世桐)、Tsung Yih Tuh (張一德) 和 Sun Tson Lian (沈仲良)。他表示 Sun Tson Lian 居住在马克姆路6/62号。刑事侦缉股警员19号和具名者于1938年11月14日下午访问了上述地址，并从 Sun Tson Lian 的母亲 Sun Wong Sz (沈王氏) 处得知，他21岁，上海人，是 Brennan Road 一家缫丝厂股东 Sun Long Chih (沈隆志) 的儿子。她在此地址已居住7年，其子就读于上海中学，并于1938年夏毕业。他的首次商业尝试是创办 Cathay Trading Company，亏损了500.00美元。他的父亲拒绝再为此 venture 提供资金，他现在正帮助父亲经营缫丝厂。母亲是 Sun Long Chih 的妾室，有可能是 Sun Long Chih 的妻子促使写了这封信。

侦探访问该地址时 Sun Tson Lian 不在家，对他居住的房间进行的表面检查未发现任何将其与此案联系起来的东西，他与母亲同住一间房。

7th November, 38.

Bomb thrown at 292 Bubbling Well Road.

At 7.40 p.m. on 6/11/38, a telephone message was received at this station from P.S. Ely reporting that a bomb had been thrown at 292 Bubbling Well Road, and requesting the services of an ambulance. The S.F.B. ambulance was summoned, and a party of Police immediately proceeded to the scene. From enquiries made by C.D.S. 345 and the undersigned, the following was ascertained.

At about 7.30 p.m. on 6/11/38 a bomb was thrown into a bar known as "Ma Jacksons Bar", situated at 292 Bubbling Well Road. The bomb landed on the floor near the end of the counter furthest from the entrance and exploded, causing injuries to the following British service men who were among the patrons present at the time.

1. Private W. Smith, No. 867009, "A" Company, Seaforth Highlanders. Leg injuries.
2. Private G. Ritchie, No. 2818942, H.Q. Company, Seaforth Highlanders. Leg injuries.
3. Private V. Sutherland, No. 2916655, "B" Company, Seaforth Highlanders. Leg injuries.
4. Private E. Duffy, No. 4456850, H.Q. Company, Seaforth Highlanders. Leg injuries.
5. Marine Newman, R.M.S. "Birmingham" Leg injuries.

The above are all detained in the British Military Hospital, Central Road.

6. Marine Ray, R.M.S. "Birmingham" Body and leg injuries.
7. Marine Pitt, R.M.S. "Birmingham" Body injuries.

These two marines are detained in the General Hospital, North Soochow Road.

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 7 1938

Seven Foreigners, Six
Chinese Hurt When
Terrorists Run Wild

Four Seaforths, Trio Of
Royal Marines Taken
To Hospital

BEER HALL NEAR
GRAND IS BOMBED

Four Hurt In Bombing
Of Western District
Gambling Den

Thirteen persons, seven foreigners and six Chinese, were injured during two terrorist bombings in Shanghai yesterday.

The seven foreigners are all British servicemen. Four are Seaforth Highlanders while three are Royal Marines of H.M.S. Birmingham.

Four of the Chinese are men, two are bar girls.

First of the two bombings occurred in a Chinese gambling den located near Yenping and Connaught Roads in Japanese occupied territory.

A terrorist tossed a bomb into one of the gambling rooms, and escaped. The missile exploded and four gamblers were wounded to varying degrees of seriousness. All were taken to the Chinese Red Cross Hospital. The time of this incident was 5.30 p.m.

Although the bombing occurred outside the Settlement, S.M.P. detectives were making inquiries in connection with the case.

Bar Room Bombed

The scene of the second bombing was "Ma" Jackson's beer hall located on Bubbling Well Road just across from the Race Course and near the Grand Theater.

A man described as a Chinese, dressed in a long gown, opened the door of the establishment and after surveying the assembled customers, most of whom were British servicemen, he tossed a "beer bottle" bomb onto the floor. Panic followed.

"Ma" Jackson's is a small establishment and the resulting damage was naturally heavy. The bomb exploded with a loud detonation, shattering the glass front window, bar mirror and damaging furniture.

When the emergency ambulances had finally completed the task of taking the wounded to the hospital, four Seaforth Highlanders, three Royal Marines and two bar girls were reported to be receiving medical treatment.

"Ma" Jackson, the owner of the establishment, escaped injury. Mrs. Jackson is Portuguese by birth and states that her late husband was an American.

Seaforth Badly Hurt

Private Sutherland, one of the Seaforths, is reported to have been rather seriously wounded. He sustained both spinal and leg cuts. Military doctors stated, however, that he will recover.

The other wounded men received only superficial glass cuts about the face, body and hands. While all were kept in the British Military Hospital last night, the majority possibly will be returned to their billets today.

The two wounded bar girls also sustained only superficial wounds and probably will be released from the hospital in a few days.

The wounded Seaforths are Privates Sutherland, Duffy, Richie and Smith. The wounded Royal Marines are Privates Newman, Ray and Pitt. The names of the two wounded Chinese girls were not reported last night.

Motive A Mystery

Detectives of Sinza Police Station in charge of the investigating are somewhat baffled in their efforts to unearth a motive for the bombing. Mrs. Jackson claims that she has no enemies and is neutral in her political views.

Interesting is the fact that the bomb used was of the same type as the bombs thrown in the Frisco Cabaret on Rue Chu Pao San and the New Deal Bar on Rue du Consulat several weeks ago.

Police are inclined to believe that the three bombings may have some connection; that disgruntled Chinese bar employees may have been responsible for all three incidents.

1938年11月7日

恐怖分子肆意妄为致七名外国人、六名中国人受伤

四名海福斯高地团士兵、三名皇家海军陆战队员被送往医院

大光明大戏院附近啤酒馆遭炸弹袭击

西区赌博窝点爆炸案四人受伤

昨日上海发生两起恐怖主义炸弹袭击事件，造成13人受伤，其中七名为外国人，六名为中国人。

这七名外国人均为英国军人。其中四人为海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）士兵，三人为“伯明翰”号（H.M.S. Birmingham）舰上的皇家海军陆战队员。

四名中国人为男性，两名为酒吧女侍。

第一起爆炸发生在位于日占区延平路（Yenping）与康纳脱路（Connaught Roads）附近的一家中国赌博窝点。

一名恐怖分子将一枚炸弹扔进其中一间赌室后逃逸。炸弹爆炸，四名赌徒不同程度受伤。所有人均被送往中国红十字会医院。此事发生时间为下午5时30分。

尽管爆炸发生在租界以外，但上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）侦探正在就此案进行调查。

酒吧遭炸

第二起爆炸现场是位于静安寺路、跑马厅对面且靠近大光明大戏院（Grand Theater）的“马”杰克逊（"Ma" Jackson）啤酒馆。

据描述，一名身穿长衫的中国男子打开店门，环顾店内聚集的顾客（其中大多为英国军人），随后将一枚“啤酒瓶”炸弹扔在地板上。现场随即陷入恐慌。

“马”杰克逊啤酒馆规模较小，因此造成的破坏自然严重。炸弹爆炸声巨大，震碎了临街玻璃窗、吧台镜子并损坏了家具。

当急救救护车最终完成将伤者送往医院的任务后，据悉有四名海福斯高地团士兵、三名皇家海军陆战队员和两名酒吧女侍正在接受医疗救治。

该店店主“马”杰克逊未受伤。杰克逊夫人生于葡萄牙，称其已故丈夫为美国人。

海福斯团士兵重伤

据悉，海福斯团士兵萨瑟兰（Sutherland）下士受伤较重。他的脊柱和腿部均有割伤。然而军医表示，他将康复。

其他受伤者仅面部、身体和手部受到玻璃浅表割伤。虽然所有人昨晚都留在英国军医院，但大多数人今天可能会返回营房。

两名受伤的酒吧女侍也仅受浅表伤，预计几天后即可出院。

受伤的海福斯团士兵为萨瑟兰（Sutherland）、达菲（Duffy）、里奇（Richie）和史密斯（Smith）下士。受伤的皇家海军陆战队员为纽曼（Newman）、雷（Ray）和皮特（Pitt）下士。昨晚未通报两名受伤中国女孩的姓名。

动机成谜

负责调查的新闸捕房侦探在探寻爆炸动机方面感到有些困惑。杰克逊夫人声称她没有仇敌，且在政治观点上保持中立。

值得注意的是，此次使用的炸弹类型与数周前在朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San）的弗里斯科歌舞厅（Frisco Cabaret）和新开河路（Rue du Consulat）的新政酒吧（New Deal Bar）被投掷的炸弹相同。

警方倾向于认为这三起爆炸案可能存在关联；不满的中国酒吧雇员可能是这三起事件的罪魁祸首。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOV 7 1938

Six Britons Injured In
Cafe Bombing

Chinese Throws Bottle Grenade in Bubbling
Well Road Bar: Seaforths, Marines and Two
Chinese Girls Taken to Hospital

THREE members of the 1st Battalion, the Seaforth Highlanders, three privates of the Royal Marine detachment aboard H.M.S. Birmingham and two Chinese girls were injured last night when a bomb was thrown through the doorway of Ma Jackson's tavern at 292 Bubbling Well Road. All the injured persons were removed to hospital and enquiries by the "North-China Daily News" at midnight elicited the information that they were in no danger. Several sailors from H.M.S. Birmingham and other members of the Seaforth Highlanders, who were in the tavern at the time, suffered slight injuries from flying glass but their condition did not warrant their removal to hospital.

The names of the injured persons are: Ptes. Sutherland, Ritchie, and Duffy of the Seaforths, Ptes. Newman, Pitt, and Ray of the Royal Marines. The first four are now detained at the British Military Hospital in Central Road, while Pitt and Ray are being treated at the General Hospital. The two girls were taken to the Red Cross Hospital.

Thrown Through Door

From eye-witness accounts of the bombing given to a "North-China Daily News" reporter, it appears that about 7.30 p.m. the door of the tavern was thrown open suddenly, a Chinese appeared on the threshold and threw something with great force into the room. Immediately there was a loud explosion as the object burst near the window and broken glass flew in all directions, injuring some soldiers and Royal Marines who were sitting directly facing the window.

In the general alarm which followed the explosion, the thrower dashed away and although he was chased by a member of the Seaforth Highlanders and a few pedestrians on the street at the time he managed to escape. Meanwhile, inside the tavern the injured people were picking themselves up from the floor where they had been hurled by the force of the detonation. Ambulances were immediately summoned and they were removed to the hospital. Pitt and Ray, who is the youngest Marine aboard the Birmingham, appeared to have suffered most and a taxi was summoned so that they could receive immediate treatment at the General Hospital.

Glass Bomb

An R.A.S.C. ambulance conveyed the other four men to the Military Hospital where they were treated by Capt. Smyth. Their wounds were stated to be superficial although each of them had lost an amount of blood. They were in no danger, however, when a "North-China Daily News" reporter visited there shortly before midnight.

All the injuries were caused by flying glass from the exploding missile which was found to be a home-made grenade fashioned out of a bottle, being an exact replica of the two bombs which were thrown in the Frisco and New Deal cabarets recently on Rue Chu Pao San. Detectives from Sinza Police station arrived on the scene shortly after the bombing and were conducting enquiries for over two hours, during which time most of the debris near the window, which had been boarded up, and had been cleared away.

No Clues

At a late hour last night, no clue as to the motive for the hurling of the missile had been unearthed and so far it remains a mystery. Military Police co-operated with the detectives as enquiries proceeded and a Shore Patrol from H.M.S. Birmingham also arrived on the scene, as the establishment was closed by order of detectives. At 9 p.m. last night a Chinese police constable stood on guard in the doorway, but it is understood that customers were allowed to enter after the departure of the detectives.

A member of the Seaforth Highlanders who was in the tavern at the time of the bombing told a "North-China Daily News" reporter that "it all happened in a flash. I saw this fellow open the door," he added "and suddenly he heaved a bottle into the room near the bar and here was a loud explosion. The girls behind the counter screamed and flying glass was everywhere."

Gave Chase

This witness continued that he ran towards the door and saw the man running across the road, when he gave chase, but owing to traffic and some pedestrians getting in the way he lost sight of him. "I went back to the tavern to see what had happened to my mates" he went on "and I found them lying about the place bleeding freely, but there was no panic."

A sailor from H.M.S. Birmingham who was at the other end of the bar when the grenade was thrown stated that it all happened so suddenly that everyone was dazed for some time. "There was a blast of hot air, the room filled with smoke, and glass and fragments from the counter flew about," he informed the reporter. "I immediately ducked as someone shouted 'bomb' but even then my fingers were cut with glass."

No Danger

From enquiries made at the General and Military hospitals it was found that the injuries to Pitt and Ray included lacerations to the body and legs, and injuries to the chest and abdomen, which will necessitate their detention in hospital. Sutherland, Ritchie, Duffy and Newman were stated to have suffered from wounds to the body and legs, the first-named being the most seriously injured of the party. No statements were taken from the men last night. The two girls' injuries were superficial and they are expected to be released immediately.

Reports that Sutherland and the two Marines at the General Hospital were in dangerous conditions proved to be false and it was stated by medical authorities that they are in no danger.

《字林西报》（North-China Daily News），
1938年11月7日

咖啡馆爆炸案致六名英国人受伤

中国人在静安寺路酒吧投掷瓶式手榴弹：海福斯团士兵、海军陆战队员及两名中国女孩被送往医院

昨晚，当一枚炸弹被扔进静安寺路292号“马”杰克逊酒馆的门口时，海福斯高地团第一营的三名成员、“伯明翰”号舰上皇家海军陆战队分遣队的三名普通士兵以及两名中国女孩受伤。所有伤者均被送往医院，《字林西报》午夜时的查询获悉，他们均无生命危险。当时在酒馆内的几名“伯明翰”号水兵和其他海福斯高地团成员因飞溅的玻璃受了轻伤，但其状况无需送医。

伤者姓名为：海福斯团的萨瑟兰（Sutherland）、里奇（Ritchie）和达菲（Duffy）下士，皇家海军陆战队的纽曼（Newman）、皮特（Pitt）和雷（Ray）下士。前四人目前羁押在中路（Central Road）的英国军医院，而皮特和雷正在广慈医院（General Hospital）接受治疗。两名女孩被送往红十字会医院。

从门口投掷

根据目击者向《字林西报》记者提供的爆炸经过，似乎大约在晚上7时30分，酒馆的门突然被推开，一名中国人出现在门槛上，用力向室内投掷某物。物体在窗户附近爆裂，立即发出巨大的爆炸声，碎玻璃四处飞溅，伤了正对着窗户坐着的几名士兵和海军陆战队员。

在随后的普遍恐慌中，投掷者飞奔逃离，尽管当时有一名海福斯高地团士兵和几名街头行人追赶，但他仍成功逃脱。与此同时，酒馆内受伤的人们正从被爆炸冲击力掀翻在地的地板上爬起来。救护车立即被召来，将他们送往医院。皮特和雷是“伯明翰”号上最年轻的海军陆战队员，似乎受伤最重，因此叫了一辆出租车，以便他们在广慈医院接受即时治疗。

玻璃炸弹

一辆皇家陆军后勤 Corps（R.A.S.C.）救护车将另外四人送往军医院，由史密斯（Smyth）上尉进行治疗。据说他们的伤口虽浅，但每人都失血不少。然而，当《字林西报》记者在午夜前不久探访时，他们已无生命危险。

所有伤害均由爆炸弹片飞溅的玻璃造成，该爆炸物被发现是用瓶子制成的自制手榴弹，与近期在朱葆三路的弗里斯科和新政歌舞厅投掷的两枚炸弹完全一样。新闸捕房的侦探在爆炸后不久抵达现场，并进行了两个多小时的调查，在此期间，窗户附近的大部分碎片（已被木板封住）已被清理。

无线索

昨晚深夜，尚未发现投掷该物体的动机线索，因此目前仍是个谜。随着调查的进行，宪兵与侦探合作，“伯明翰”号的岸上巡逻队也抵达现场，因为该场所奉侦探之命关闭。昨晚9时，一名中国巡捕站在门口守卫，但据悉侦探离开后允许顾客进入。

一名爆炸发生时在酒馆内的海福斯高地团成员告诉《字林西报》记者：“一切都发生在一瞬间。我看见这家伙打开门，”他补充道，“突然他把一个瓶子扔进靠近吧台的房间里，接着是一声巨大的爆炸。柜台后面的女孩们尖叫起来，玻璃碎片到处都是。”

展开追捕

这位证人继续说，他跑向门口，看见那人跑过马路，他便追了上去，但由于交通和一些行人挡路，他失去了那人的踪迹。“我回到酒馆看看我的伙伴们怎么样了，”他接着说，“我发现他们躺在各处，血流不止，但没有出现恐慌。”

当手榴弹被投掷时，一名来自“伯明翰”号的水兵正处在吧台的另一端，他表示一切发生得太突然，所有人都愣神了一段时间。“一股热浪袭来，房间里充满了烟雾，柜台上的玻璃和碎片四处飞散，”他告诉记者。“当有人喊‘炸弹’时，我立即蹲下，但即使这样，我的手指还是被玻璃划伤了。”

无生命危险

经在广慈医院和军医院查询得知，皮特和雷的伤势包括身体和腿部撕裂伤，以及胸部和腹部受伤，这需要他们留院治疗。据悉，萨瑟兰、里奇、达菲和纽曼遭受了身体和腿部创伤，其中萨瑟兰是这群人中受伤最严重的。昨晚未对这些人进行录供。两名女孩的伤势较浅，预计将立即获释。

有关萨瑟兰和广慈医院的两名海军陆战队员情况危急的报道被证实为不实，医务当局表示他们并无生命危险。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

NOV 7 1938

Bomb Hurled
In Bubbling
Well Rd. Bar

Four Seaforth Privates,
Three Royal Marines,
Two Girls Injured

Seven British servicemen and two Chinese girls sustained various degrees of injury when a home-made type of grenade was thrown into Ma Jackson's Bar at 292 Bubbling Well Road, opposite the Race Course, at about 7.30 yesterday evening.

Detectives of the Sinza Road Police Station, who rushed to the scene of the latest bombing outrage, at midnight were still at a loss to ascertain the motive for the crime. Employees of the popular British bar stated last night that they saw an unknown Chinese open the front door of the establishment, stand there for a few seconds and then hurl the explosive into the middle of the bar room.

The explosion shook the whole premises, breaking the front plate glass window and doing considerable damage to the glassware and furniture in the bar itself, in addition to injuring nine persons.

Among those injured were four members of the First Battalion, the Seaforth Highlanders;
Private Sutherland,
Private Richie,
Private Duffy,
Private Smith.

Three Royal Marines off H.M.S. Birmingham were also among the injured:
Marine Newman,
Marine Ray,
Marine Pitt.

Two Chinese girls were further injured, one of them seriously, both being taken to St. Elizabeth's Hospital, where one of them was detained for treatment. Among the servicemen, Private Sutherland was among the most seriously injured, sustaining injuries to his spine and leg.

Excitement Reigns

Excitement reigned along Bubbling Well Road as the sound of the explosion and breaking glass was heard, followed by the screams of the injured, to be followed a few minutes later by the arrival of the police and the ambulance. Large numbers of servicemen in the vicinity rushed into the barroom, thinking that a fight had broken out. They remained to assist the injured.

Ma Jackson, the proprietress of the popular bar, was at a loss last night to find any reason why a grenade should have been thrown at her establishment.

It will be recalled that about a month ago, a similar type of grenade was hurled at two establishments along the famous "Blood Alley." The places attacked were the Frisco Cabaret and New Deal Bar.

Another Bombing

Yet another bombing outrage occurred earlier in the day, a tin type of grenade exploding in the Yuen Kee Gambling Club on Yenping Road, near Connaught Road, outside Settlement limits. Four Chinese sustained injuries in this explosion, all being taken by the Shanghai Fire Brigade ambulance to the Red Cross Hospital. Two of them were released after their wounds had been attended to, while the two others, more seriously injured, were detained. This explosion occurred shortly before 5.30 p.m., and the grenade was believed to have been left on the premises in revenge.

1938年11月7日

炸弹投掷于
静安寺路酒吧

四名海福尔团列兵、
三名皇家海军陆战队员、
两名女子受伤

昨晚约7时30分，一枚自制手榴弹被投入位于静安寺路292号、跑马厅对面的“马杰克逊酒吧”（Ma Jackson's Bar），导致七名英国军人和两名中国女孩受到不同程度的伤害。

新闸路警察局的侦探迅速赶赴这起最新爆炸暴行的现场，直至午夜仍无法查明犯罪动机。这家颇受欢迎的英式酒吧的员工昨晚称，他们看见一名身份不明的中国人打开店门，在那里站了几秒钟，然后将爆炸物扔进酒吧大厅中央。

爆炸震动了整个场所，震碎了前门的平板玻璃窗，并对酒吧内的玻璃器皿和家具造成了相当大的损坏，此外还致使九人受伤。

伤者中包括第一营海福尔高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的四名列兵：
萨瑟兰列兵（Private Sutherland），
里奇列兵（Private Richie），
达菲列兵（Private Duffy），
史密斯列兵（Private Smith）。

来自皇家海军“伯明翰”号（H.M.S. Birmingham）的三名皇家海军陆战队员也在伤者之列：
纽曼陆战队员（Marine Newman），
雷陆战队员（Marine Ray），
皮特陆战队员（Marine Pitt）。

另有两名中国女孩受伤，其中一人伤势严重，两人均被送往圣伊丽莎白医院（St. Elizabeth's Hospital），其中一人留院治疗。在军人伤者中，萨瑟兰列兵伤势最为严重，脊柱和腿部受伤。

一片哗然

当爆炸声和玻璃破碎声传来，随后是伤者的尖叫声，静安寺路上一片哗然。几分钟后，警察和救护车抵达。附近的大量军人冲进酒吧，以为发生了斗殴。他们留下来协助救治伤者。

这家颇受欢迎酒吧的女老板马杰克逊（Ma Jackson）昨晚对有人向她的店铺投掷手榴弹的原因感到困惑不解。

值得回顾的是，大约一个月前，类似类型的手榴弹曾被投掷到著名的“血巷”（Blood Alley）沿线的两家场所。受袭地点为弗里斯科歌舞厅（Frisco Cabaret）和新政酒吧（New Deal Bar）。

另一起爆炸案

当天早些时候又发生了一起爆炸暴行，一枚铁制手榴弹在界外康纳路（Connaught Road）附近的延平路（Yenping Road）元记赌博俱乐部（Yuen Kee Gambling Club）爆炸。四名中国人在此次爆炸中受伤，均由上海救火会救护车送往红十字会医院。其中两人在伤口得到处理后获释，另外两人伤势较重，被留院观察。这次爆炸发生在下午5时30分前不久，据信这枚手榴弹是被留在该场所以进行报复。

At 3.15 p.m. on the 12-3-38 a telephone message was
received from the D.C. (Crime) stating that he had
received a report from Mr. T. Thomas Cheyne (Chinese),
Advisor to the Consolidated Tax Bureau of Kiangsu, Chekiang
& Anhwei, to the effect that he had received information
from the Japanese Military Police that Anti-Japanese
elements might attempt to bomb the Bureau's offices at 230
Kiukiang Road, between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. on the 12-3-38.
Arrangements were immediately made with the Officer i/c
for F.S. Albon and three C.P.C.s to be detailed for special
observation duty in the vicinity of the Bureau's office.
Accompanied by C.D.S.s 56 & 111, the undersigned
interviewed Mr. T.T. Cheyne, who was unable to furnish any
information additional to that supplied to the D.C.(Crime).
The above detectives and F.S. Albon remained on duty
in the vicinity until the Bureau closed at 6 p.m. at which
time nothing of a suspicious nature had been noted.
The three C.P.C.s were withdrawn at 7 p.m. and replaced
by one C.P.C. who remained on duty until 9 p.m. at which
time he also was withdrawn.
Mr. T.T. Cheyne requested that a Police guard of three
C.P.C.s be posted for observation duty in the vicinity
during the next few days. He was informed that this
request would be brought to the notice of the Officer i/c
